variants.omim_name: GRIN2D, NOVEL HETEROZYGOUS GRIN2D MISSENSE VARIANTS

records.label: Two unrelated children with GRIN2D p.Val667Ile

phenotypes.text: seizures refractory to conventional antiepileptic medications

quotes: Here, we report a de novo recurrent heterozygous missense mutation-c.1999G>A (p.Val667Ile)-in a NMDAR gene previously unrecognized to harbor disease-causing mutations, GRIN2D, identified by exome and candidate panel sequencing in two unrelated children with epileptic encephalopathy.
Because both individuals' seizures had proven refractory to conventional antiepileptic medications
The older proband subsequently developed refractory status epilepticus, with dramatic electroclinical improvement upon treatment with ketamine and magnesium.

records.label: Three unrelated patients with GRIN2D missense variants
quotes: we identified by whole exome sequencing novel heterozygous GRIN2D missense variants in three unrelated patients with severe developmental delay and intractable epilepsy.

notes.statement: Tsuchida et al. (2018) found that the residues changed by the three GRIN2D variants were highly conserved across vertebrates and among the four GluN2 subunits. Based on protein structure, they predicted that all three variants probably impair GluN2D function, either by affecting how subunits interact or by altering channel gating.
quotes: All altered residues were highly conserved across vertebrates and among the four GluN2 subunits.
Structural consideration indicated that all three variants are probably to impair GluN2D function, either by affecting intersubunit interaction or altering channel gating activity.

notes.statement: Tsuchida et al. (2018) compared their 3 patients with the 2 previously reported patients who had a recurrent de novo GRIN2D variant and found that all of them had similar clinical features.
quotes: We assessed the clinical features of our three cases and compared them to those of the two previously reported GRIN2D variant cases, and found that they all show similar clinical features.

notes.statement: Tsuchida et al. (2018) suggested that a genetic diagnosis of GluN2-related disorders may be clinically useful when considering drug therapy that targets NMDA receptors.
quotes: Genetic diagnosis for GluN2-related disorders may be clinically useful when considering drug therapy targeting NMDA receptors.

notes.statement: Li et al. (2016) found that the GluN2D p.Val667Ile substitution lies in the M3 transmembrane domain, which is involved in channel gating. They showed it was a gain-of-function mutation: it doubled glutamate and glycine potency, raised channel open probability 6-fold, made the receptor less sensitive to negative modulators such as extracellular protons, and prolonged deactivation after glutamate removal.
quotes: The resulting GluN2D p.Val667Ile exchange occurs in the M3 transmembrane domain involved in channel gating.

This gain-of-function mutation increases glutamate and glycine potency by 2-fold, increases channel open probability by 6-fold, and reduces receptor sensitivity to endogenous negative modulators such as extracellular protons.
Moreover, this mutation prolongs the deactivation time course after glutamate removal, which controls the synaptic time course.

notes.statement: Li et al. (2016) found that transfecting cultured neurons with human GRIN2D cDNA carrying c.1999G>A caused dendritic swelling and neuronal cell death. They took this as suggestive of excitotoxicity from NMDAR overactivation.
quotes: Transfection of cultured neurons with human GRIN2D cDNA harboring c.1999G>A leads to dendritic swelling and neuronal cell death, suggestive of excitotoxicity mediated by NMDAR over-activation.

notes.statement: Li et al. (2016) tested the mutant receptors in vitro for sensitivity to FDA-approved NMDAR antagonists and then gave oral memantine to both children, with mild to moderate improvement in seizure burden and development. The older proband later developed refractory status epilepticus, which improved dramatically on ketamine and magnesium. The authors suggested NMDAR antagonists could be useful as adjuvant therapy for GRIN2D gain-of-function mutations.
quotes: Based on these results, oral memantine was administered to both children, with resulting mild to moderate improvement in seizure burden and development.
The older proband subsequently developed refractory status epilepticus, with dramatic electroclinical improvement upon treatment with ketamine and magnesium.
Overall, these results suggest that NMDAR antagonists can be useful as adjuvant epilepsy therapy in individuals with GRIN2D gain-of-function mutations.
